discovery_source: Banking: payment-rail compliance programs (Nacha Operating Rules, Reg E, UCC 4A, card network rules, PCI DSS)
industry_analogy: Bank treasury 'rules of the road' matrices kept by corporate originators
why_no_predecessor: OB-43/OB-44/OB-45 record rail regimes as single rows without the sponsor's role per rail or a control link.
business_problem: Sponsor does not know which rail duties bind it as Originator, payee, merchant or holder before going live.
statement: The system MUST maintain a versioned RailObligation register with one row per (rail, direction, sponsor role ∈ {Originator, ThirdPartySender, Payee, Merchant, Holder, BankCustomer}, obligation), each carrying source (statute, regulation, network rule, bank contract, sponsor policy), citation, effective date, binding class, linked control ID, owner and counsel status; the PAY-DEF-001 production gate for a rail MUST fail while any binding row for that rail and role lacks an implemented, tested control. Default roles (XID-BNK-005): the sponsor is Originator of record on sponsor-titled accounts under its own ODFI agreement; the platform operator is a Third-Party Service Provider, never a Third-Party Sender, and holds no funds.
rationale: Turns diffuse 'contractual' rows into testable go-live prerequisites; separates binding duties from practice.
evidence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/ucc/4A/4A-211 (accessed 2026-11-23) [primary, read: cancellation after acceptance only with receiving-bank agreement; beneficiary bank limited to unauthorized/duplicate/mistake]

https://nacha.org/rules/supplementing-fraud-detection-standards-web-debits and https://www.nacha.org/sites/default/files/2020-06/End_User_Briefing_Account_Validation_FINAL.pdf (accessed 2026-11-23) [search-result summary of Nacha pages; not opened in full]

discovery_source: Banking: Nacha 2026 risk-based fraud monitoring (Phase 2 effective 2026-06-19/22)
industry_analogy: Corporate Originator fraud programs for credit-push payments
why_no_predecessor: REQ-X-005/GRT-017 cover destination evidence but not a documented, annually reviewed program for entries authorized under False Pretenses.
business_problem: BEC and charity-impersonation redirect grant credits; Nacha requires a documented risk-based program.
statement: For each sponsor that originates ACH entries (directly or via a Third-Party Sender), the system MUST maintain a documented FraudMonitoringProgram covering at least: destination-change after-the-fact review, first payment to a new destination, payment-amount anomaly versus the recipient's history, request-channel provenance for any bank-detail change, and debit-origination anomalies; each rule MUST have a version, owner, risk rationale and outcome metrics; the program MUST record a completed review at least every 12 months and block new ACH origination when the last review is older than 12 months plus a configured grace period.

discovery_source: Payments/billing: Reg E preauthorized transfer authorization (12 CFR 1005.10(b),(d))
why_no_predecessor: Recurring requirements cover grant schedules only; no requirement captures consumer debit authorizations.
business_problem: Recurring donor debits without retrievable authorizations violate Reg E (payee duty) and lose R10 disputes.
statement: Before the first recurring debit from a consumer account (ACH or debit card), the system MUST capture an authorization signed or similarly authenticated by the consumer that states amount (or range), frequency, start date, debiting entity name and revocation method; MUST deliver a copy to the consumer and record delivery evidence; MUST send notice of any varying amount outside the authorized range at least 10 days before the debit; MUST honor revocation for all occurrences not yet sent to the ODFI; and MUST retain the authorization for at least 2 years after termination or longer per retention policy.
rationale: Binding on the payee; inexpensive to implement in intake.

discovery_source: Payments: Nacha WEB debit account validation rule (enforceable 2022-03-19)
why_no_predecessor: Contribution intake requirements predate this control analysis.

discovery_source: Merchant processing: card network dispute/chargeback lifecycle
why_no_predecessor: REQ-X-009 models single-step returns; card disputes are two-phase with deadlines and can reverse twice.
business_problem: Card chargebacks reverse accepted, acknowledged and possibly granted gifts.
statement: For card contributions the system MUST model DisputeLifecycle {Inquiry, DisputeOpened(provisional debit), EvidenceDue(deadline), Represented, Won(re-credit), Lost(final), Accepted} linked to the original contribution; on DisputeOpened it MUST record a ReturnedContributionExposure per RR-REQ-X-009-r1, reduce capacity by the disputed amount, and open an acknowledgment-correction task if acknowledged; it MUST classify the event as InvoluntaryReversal (not a refund under UNB-RCN-FIN-013); a decision to represent MUST be made by an authorized human when amount ≥ the sponsor ContestThreshold, else follow the sponsor default (Accept or Represent); card contributions MUST remain Provisional for capacity purposes for the sponsor-configured card window.
rationale: Card disputes are common in low-friction giving and unmodeled.
evidence: https://usa.visa.com/dam/VCOM/global/support-legal/documents/faq-apr-disputes.pdf (accessed 2026-11-23) [search-result summary: 120 days, some reasons up to 540 days]

discovery_source: Payments: Nacha return-rate thresholds and reinitiation rules
why_no_predecessor: Return handling covers individual returns, not portfolio rates or reinitiation constraints.
business_problem: Excess returns trigger ODFI inquiry and loss of origination.
statement: The system MUST compute, per Originator identity, rolling 60-day unauthorized (R05, R07, R10, R11, R29, R51), administrative (R02, R03, R04) and overall debit return rates; MUST alert at configurable fractions of Nacha thresholds (0.5%, 3.0%, 15.0%) and suspend new debit origination for a channel exceeding a sponsor-configured hard limit; MUST permit reinitiation only for returns coded R01 or R09 (and R02/R03/R04 only after corrective action), with identical Company Name, Company ID and amount and 'RETRY PYMT' description, within the configured count and window; and MUST NOT reinitiate any unauthorized-coded return without a new authorization.

discovery_source: Merchant processing: gross/fee/net settlement and donor-covered fees
why_no_predecessor: FeeBase covers fees on funds; inbound processor fees and donor fee coverage are undefined.
business_problem: Acknowledgments and cash reconciliation diverge when processors settle net.
statement: For every processor-settled contribution the system MUST record gross amount charged to the donor (including any donor-elected fee coverage), the processor fee actually assessed, and net settled, linked to the payout batch and bank credit; the contribution credited to the fund and stated on the acknowledgment MUST be determined by a CPA/counsel-approved FeeCoveragePolicy (default: gross charged is the contribution; processor fee posted as sponsor or fund expense per policy); and a payout batch MUST NOT reconcile unless Σgross − Σfees − Σreversals = net payout = bank credit. Default FeeCoveragePolicy (XID-BNK-002): the gross amount charged is the contribution and the acknowledged amount; the fund is credited gross and the processor fee posts as a separate fund expense line.
rationale: Correct acknowledgments and three-way processor reconciliation.

acceptance_criteria.then: the batch stays ExceptionOpen with the delta and no gift is marked Settled from that batch

acceptance_criteria.given: a donor gives $100 and elects to cover a $3.20 fee, paying $103.20
acceptance_criteria.then: the acknowledgment states $103.20, the fund is credited $103.20 and a $3.20 processing-fee expense line posts to the fund

simplest_valid_alternative: Treat fees as fund-charged only (no donor coverage).
decision_rationale: Gross recognition is the conventional and auditable choice.

discovery_source: Brokerage clearing: DTC delivery matching for securities gifts
why_no_predecessor: Unidentified deposits are listed (UNB-GAP-013) and AI matching proposed, but no deterministic intent-to-delivery contract exists.
business_problem: Gifts attributed to wrong donor or delayed.
statement: Securities gift intake MUST collect a GiftIntent (donor, fund, security identifier, quantity, delivering DTC participant number, expected date); incoming custody receipts MUST be matched deterministically on (security identifier, quantity, delivering participant, date window); exactly one match MUST auto-link; zero or multiple matches MUST place the position in Unidentified suspense with no fund credit or acknowledgment; partial quantity MUST link as PartiallyReceived; user-facing copy MUST NOT describe gifts as 'ACATS transfers'.
rationale: Most noncash gifts are DTC-eligible securities; straight-through matching removes manual work.
evidence: https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/rulebooks/finra-rules/11870 (accessed 2026-11-23) [primary, read: ACATS customer account transfer; title-mismatch exception; 1+3 business days]

discovery_source: Banking: corporate treasury 'every debit authorized' daily control
why_no_predecessor: TVR-PAY-004 is preventive; rev3 B19 covers custodians not bank debits.
business_problem: Out-of-band portal payments bypass platform controls.
statement: Every business day the system MUST ingest bank activity for each sponsor disbursement, clearing and operating account linked to Unbound and match every debit to exactly one authorized platform instruction or to a configured expected-debit class (bank fee, sweep, return); any unmatched debit MUST open a high-severity incident within one hour of ingestion, notify two independent sponsor roles and place a protective hold on further releases from that account until an authorized human classifies it; ACH debit block or filter status for disbursement accounts MUST be recorded and attested quarterly. Grant disbursement accounts MUST carry an ACH debit block allowing only named bank-fee company IDs; processors MUST settle to a separate contribution clearing account where only the processor's company ID may debit (XID-BNK-008).
rationale: Detective control complements TVR-PAY-004 and covers bank-portal compromise.

acceptance_criteria.then: an incident opens, releases from that account are held, and two roles are notified

acceptance_criteria.given: a monthly bank service charge
acceptance_criteria.then: it matches the expected-debit class and no incident opens

acceptance_criteria.given: bank activity feed missing for a business day
acceptance_criteria.then: a FeedMissing exception opens and the account is marked Unverified

acceptance_criteria.given: a processor chargeback debit
acceptance_criteria.then: it posts only against the contribution clearing account and any attempt against a disbursement account is returned by the bank block

failure_conditions: Feed gap treated as zero activity
security_compliance: Bank credentials stored per sponsor; read-only feed.
ai_automation: Deterministic match; AI may explain likely origin; humans classify.
ui_implications: Treasury view with unmatched debits first.
testing_requirements: Fixtures: out-of-band wire, fee, missing feed.
priority_justification: Prevents material loss from the main disclosed fraud vector.
simplest_valid_alternative: Daily manual review of bank activity export.
decision_rationale: Automated match is cheap once feeds exist.
open_questions: EXT-03: what bank portals export daily.

discovery_source: Payments: payment-class x rail eligibility matrix
why_no_predecessor: REQ-X-083 is grant-centric and silent on instant rails and non-grant payment classes.
business_problem: Ambiguous rail use for refunds, fees, transfers; irrevocable rails used without extra controls.
statement: The system MUST maintain a versioned RailEligibility matrix keyed by (payment class ∈ {Grant, SponsorToSponsorTransfer, ReturnOfUnacceptedProperty, ProcessorRefundOfDuplicate, VendorPayment, InternalFeeTransfer, InvestmentSettlement}, rail, direction) with fields Allowed, IrreversibilityClass {Reversible, RequestOnly, Irrevocable}, per-payment and daily limits, and extra controls; commands MUST reject any payment whose class/rail is not Allowed; Irrevocable or RequestOnly rails MUST require independent destination confirmation per UNB-RCN-GRT-017 for each payment above the configured threshold; instant rails (RTP/FedNow) MUST default to not Allowed for Grant until a sponsor decision enables them; InternalFeeTransfer MUST be a ledger journal with no external rail.
rationale: One table makes rail use explicit and testable across contributions, grants, fees and investments.
evidence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/ucc/4A/4A-211 (accessed 2026-11-23) [primary, read: cancellation after acceptance only with receiving-bank agreement; beneficiary bank limited to unauthorized/duplicate/mistake]
https://www.frbservices.org/news/communications/111225-fednow-transaction-limit-increase (accessed 2026-11-23) [search-result summary: FedNow network limit $10m from 2025-11-12; RTP $10m]

acceptance_criteria.then: independent destination confirmation evidence is required before dispatch

acceptance_criteria.given: a fee charge
acceptance_criteria.then: no payment instruction is created

discovery_source: Banking/processing: per-rail cost-to-serve drivers
industry_analogy: Bank activity-based costing / account analysis statements
why_no_predecessor: Metrics cover STP and human touches but not rail-specific cost facts.
business_problem: Economics model cannot price rails or exceptions.
statement: Every contribution, payment, return, dispute, reissue and payment exception event MUST emit a CostDriver fact {sponsor, payment class, rail, provider, external fee amount and source (actual invoice/report vs schedule vs illustrative), physical items (checks printed, postage, lockbox items), manual touch count and handling minutes, exception type} that the economics component consumes; CostDriver facts MUST NOT alter ledger balances and illustrative costs MUST be labelled as such.

acceptance_criteria.then: schedule-based CostDriver amounts are superseded by actuals with lineage

discovery_source: Banking: positive pay issue-file gate and payee-name positive pay
why_no_predecessor: RCF-GRT-020 flagged missing issue files; no gap requirement adopted.
business_problem: Altered/stolen checks paid by bank.
statement: A check MUST NOT move from Printed to Released-for-mail until the bank has acknowledged an issue file containing its number, amount, issue date and (where the bank supports it) payee name; positive-pay exception decisions MUST default to Return; a Pay decision on an exception MUST require an authorized human who did not issue the check and recorded evidence; voids MUST be transmitted and acknowledged before reissue (per GRT-005).
rationale: Makes positive pay effective; payee-name matching addresses check washing.

discovery_source: Accounting/fund accounting: community-foundation audited statements (agency endowments as liabilities)

parent_capability: Account-type classification and posting policy selection
why_no_predecessor: UNB-RCN-ENT-011 classifies DAF vs non-DAF for excise-tax purposes but does not select accounting treatment; no requirement mentions agency or pass-through funds.
business_problem: Hybrid and embedded sponsors hold money for other nonprofits or pass designated gifts through; booking them as contributions overstates revenue, net assets and possibly Schedule D.
statement: Every account type in the account-type register MUST carry a CPA-approved AccountingTreatment of exactly one of {Contribution-WithoutDonorRestriction, Contribution-WithDonorRestriction, AgencyLiability, PassThroughLiability}. Receipts into an AgencyLiability or PassThroughLiability account MUST post to a liability (funds held for others) and MUST NOT increase contribution revenue, DAF counts or Schedule D Part I aggregates; payouts from such accounts MUST reduce the liability and MUST NOT be recorded as grant expense. An account type without an approved AccountingTreatment MUST NOT accept receipts. applicability: tenant-configurable (required for hybrid, institutional, embedded and high-volume-low-balance models)

discovery_source: Accounting: ASU 2018-08 / ASC 720-25 resource-provider recognition; audited sponsor grant policy
industry_analogy: Grantmaker accounting for contributions made (foundations, community foundations)
why_no_predecessor: UNB-ACC-007 lists lifecycle states; CANONICAL line 60 says recognition 'depends on' policy; OD-19 is an open decision without a parameter or evidence rule.
business_problem: Year-end grant surges create approved-but-unpaid grants whose period and amount must be consistent across GAAP, Schedule D and donor statements; conditional grants need different timing.
statement: Each sponsor book MUST declare one GrantRecognitionPoint from {ApprovalCommunicatedToGrantee (default), PaymentReleased}, effective-dated and CPA-approved; PaymentReleased MAY be declared only where payment is the first communication of the grant to the grantee. The platform MUST send the approval notice to the grantee automatically on sponsor approval, and the posting rule MUST recognize grant expense and grants payable for an unconditional grant only when the communication record (timestamp, channel, recipient) or, for PaymentReleased, the payment release ID exists. Sponsor approval without communication MUST NOT be recognized (an intention, not a promise to give). A grant whose terms contain both a barrier and a right of return or release, or whose terms are ambiguous, MUST be recorded as ConditionalGrant with no expense until a recorded BarrierMet or Waived event. At each period end, Unbound MUST produce a cutoff register listing grants approved but not communicated, communicated but not paid, and conditional, with their recognition status.
rationale: ASC 720-25-25-1 recognizes contributions made in the period made; ASU 2018-08 condition test and presumption; one audited sponsor recognizes unconditional grants on approval.
evidence: https://storage.fasb.org/ASU_2018-08.pdf (accessed 2026-11-23): ASC 958-605-25-5A..5F as amended (condition = barrier + right of return/release; ambiguous stipulations 'shall be presumed to be' conditional); ASC 720-25-25-1 ('Contributions made shall be recognized as expenses in the period made'; unconditional promises to give cash recognized as payables); effective for contributions made, non-PBE, annual periods beginning after Dec 15, 2019

discovery_source: Accounting/audit: event-sourced ledger adversarial review
industry_analogy: Subledger-to-GL interface controls; independent recomputation in fund administration
why_no_predecessor: UNB-NAV-044/UNB-IMM-005 require deterministic rebuild but treat rebuild output as the result, not as a check against persisted journals.
business_problem: A rebuild under changed code or policy can produce different numbers than the ledger the auditor tested.
statement: Posted journals MUST be persisted as authoritative records and MUST NOT be regenerated from source events. discovery_source: Accounting: ASC 250 accounting changes and error corrections
why_no_predecessor: ACC-MDL-010 covers late discoveries; no requirement classifies posting-rule changes.
business_problem: Posting rules will change (recognition point, fee treatment, valuation policy); each change needs the right mechanism.
statement: Every posting-rule version change and every correction of a posted error MUST carry an AccountingChangeRecord classified by an authorized controller as ChangeInPrinciple, ChangeInEstimate or ErrorCorrection, with materiality assessment and CPA approval reference. ChangeInPrinciple MUST produce a cumulative-effect adjustment to opening net assets of the earliest presented period and recast comparative reports as separately versioned 'as adjusted' reports while preserving 'as originally issued' reports; ChangeInEstimate MUST apply prospectively from its effective date with no adjustment to prior periods; ErrorCorrection MUST be booked either as a prior-period adjustment with restated comparatives or in the current period, as recorded in the classification. No classification MUST cause existing posted journals to be edited or re-posted.
rationale: Distinguishes the three ASC 250 mechanisms and prevents re-posting history as a side effect of rule versioning.

discovery_source: Call centers: interaction vs case vs back-office transaction separation (general industry practice; RCF-PLT-025)
industry_analogy: Contact-center interaction record vs ticket vs billing transaction
why_no_predecessor: ADM-015/016, AIN-009 and REQ-X-048 each assume a container but none defines the boundary between contact, case, transaction and exception.

statement: Unbound MUST record every inbound or outbound human interaction as a Contact (channel, principal or 'unidentified', assurance level, reason code, linked subjects, outcome, linked case if any). discovery_source: Subscription billing: proration and minimum fees; daf-landscape fee schedules
industry_analogy: SaaS/AUM billing proration and minimum-fee true-up
why_no_predecessor: UNB-RCN-FIN-005 fixes the fee base but not how a period is segmented or how a minimum interacts with a small or closing fund.
business_problem: Funds open, close, transfer, split or change schedule mid-period; minimum fees can exceed small balances; migrations double-charge (TVS-308).
statement: The fee engine MUST compute every fund-level fee daily on the daily balance of the declared FeeBase, using actual/365 (actual/366 in leap years) unless the schedule version declares otherwise, and MUST post the computed fee once per assessment period declared in the schedule (monthly or quarterly), not daily. The computation MUST segment at each of: fund activation, schedule-version effective date, program transfer, successor split or merge, closure trigger and migration cutover; each segment uses the schedule version and fee base in effect for that segment. A minimum fee MUST be prorated by the same day count over the days the fund was billable. Grantable capacity MUST subtract fees computed but not yet posted. The assessed amount MUST NOT exceed the fund's available balance net of reservations and approved-unpaid grants at assessment; any shortfall MUST be recorded as a waived amount with reason MinimumShortfall and MUST NOT create a receivable from any donor or participant. Recomputing any assessed fee from stored inputs MUST reproduce it exactly. The daily computation MUST run in chunks so that no transaction locks more than 5,000 fund rows, and concurrent grant approvals MUST stay within their latency SLO while it runs (benchmark report 18: a single-transaction batch stalled approvals up to 347 ms at 100,000 funds and about 12 s at 1.42 million).
rationale: Removes the main sources of fee disputes and negative balances while keeping fees reproducible for SCTRL-032.

discovery_source: CRM campaigns: CAN-SPAM, TCPA in white-label
why_no_predecessor: UNB-RCN-PLT-002 has consent basis but not sender entity, commercial classification, opt-out processing or nonprofit vs for-profit sender regime.
business_problem: In white-label programs the 'sender' may be a for-profit partner or the nonprofit sponsor, changing which rules apply; opt-outs must be honored within 10 business days.
statement: Each message type MUST declare a primary-purpose class (Commercial, TransactionalOrRelationship, MandatoryLegal, Security) and a sender legal entity with its entity type (tax-exempt nonprofit or other). Every Commercial email MUST carry the sender's valid physical postal address and a functioning opt-out that remains operable for at least 30 days after sending; an opt-out MUST be applied to all Commercial sends for that sender entity within 10 business days, and suppression lists MUST be keyed by sender entity. Automated or prerecorded voice or SMS messages that include an advertisement MUST NOT be sent without consent recorded at the level required for the sender's entity type (prior express written consent unless counsel records the nonprofit rule applies). Opt-outs MUST NOT suppress MandatoryLegal, Security or TransactionalOrRelationship messages. Decided defaults: promotional email about DAF services is Commercial; in white-label programs the sender is the entity named in the From line, contractually designated as the single sender (XID-CRM-001). Automated or prerecorded calls and texts sent by or on behalf of the tax-exempt sponsor require at least prior express consent; those sent on behalf of a for-profit partner or advertising a for-profit's services require prior express written consent (XID-REG-003; 47 CFR 64.1200).

why_no_predecessor: ADM-021 covers advisor changes initiated by donors, not the advisor changing firms.
business_problem: When a professional advisor leaves a firm, firm-scoped access and fee arrangements must end; the donor decides who continues.
statement: A professional-advisor relationship MUST be scoped to the pair (individual advisor, firm). discovery_source: Enterprise SaaS tenant offboarding contrasted with HSA/IRA trustee-to-trustee transfer; daf-landscape vendor/program switching evidence
industry_analogy: Program-level portability (HSA custodian change, 529 program manager change) where accounts follow the distributor.
why_no_predecessor: RR-UNB-WF-014-r1 covers one donor-recommended transfer; RCF-ENT-012 separates partner exit as its own process but no requirement defines it; TVF-135 leaves partner-federated donors without sponsor credentials.
business_problem: When a distribution partner (wealth firm, institutional program) leaves sponsor A for sponsor B, it expects its donors' funds to follow. The funds are sponsor A's property; moving them by data operation would breach sponsor A's exclusive legal control.
statement: A distribution-partner exit MUST be processed as a PartnerExit case with states Notified > DonorOutreach > ElectionsCollected > TransfersProposed > SponsorDecided > TransfersExecuted > Reconciled > Closed. Funds MUST move to another sponsor only as individual outbound transfer grants under RR-UNB-WF-014-r1, each with a recorded recommendation from an authorized advisor of that fund and a decision by sponsor A (which MAY be a sponsor-approved batch policy); no fund MUST change LegalSponsorId by data migration. Funds whose advisors do not recommend transfer MUST remain with sponsor A, with access through a sponsor-direct credential provisioned before the partner's federation ends, and with servicing reassigned to sponsor A or a successor partner. Partner access, subscriptions and API clients MUST terminate at the exit effective time while accepted recommendations continue under sponsor review. The case MUST reconcile: count and value of funds elected, transferred, declined and remaining, with zero unexplained difference. A sponsor-approved batch policy is the written exercise of sponsor A's discretion and MUST be applied per fund: each transfer has its own decision record citing the policy and its hold and sanctions checks; sponsor A MAY decline or condition individual transfers; a contractual pre-commitment that removes sponsor discretion MUST NOT be accepted (XID-SAS-002).
rationale: Protects §4966 exclusive legal control while making partner moves, which the market shows are frequent, operationally possible.

discovery_source: Site reliability engineering: SLIs, SLOs and error-budget policy
industry_analogy: Google SRE workbook error budget policy.
why_no_predecessor: UNB-TEN-015 and ADM-033 call for targets/SLAs but define no SLIs, measurement, budget or consequence; nothing separates availability budgets from financial correctness.
business_problem: Without SLOs there is no objective basis for partner SLAs, service credits or pausing feature releases when reliability degrades.
statement: Unbound MUST define SLIs and SLOs for at least: grant recommendation acceptance latency and availability, donor portal availability, partner API availability, statement availability by deadline, payment dispatch timeliness after release, and webhook delivery latency; each measured per tenant and in aggregate over rolling 28 days. discovery_source: Workforce IAM vs customer IAM separation in B2B2C SaaS
industry_analogy: Separate identity realms (workforce, partner workforce, consumer).
why_no_predecessor: REQ-X-057 requires one identity framework and CTL-033 distinguishes workforce vs donor authentication, but no requirement keeps the principal populations in distinct realms.
business_problem: A single store mixing operator staff, sponsor staff and donors lets a donor credential reach staff functions and makes partner exit a mass-recovery event.
statement: Every principal MUST belong to exactly one realm: PlatformWorkforce, SponsorWorkforce (per tenant, federated or local), PartnerWorkforce (per partner, federated), Customer (donor, advisor, successor, charity user) or Workload (service and AI agent principals). why_no_predecessor: REQ-X-038 enforces holds inside the platform; TVS-484 shows a partner destroying data under a deletion attestation during a subpoena; holds do not propagate to processors, partners, print vendors or migration targets.

statement: A LegalHold MUST list, at creation and on any scope change, every registered processor, distribution partner and deployment cell holding in-scope data, and MUST send each a preservation notice through the outbox with acknowledgment tracking; unacknowledged notices MUST escalate after 5 business days. discovery_source: ERP general-ledger period close; PostgreSQL isolation semantics
industry_analogy: ERP: soft/hard close with period locks; postings dated into a closed period route to prior-period adjustment
why_no_predecessor: UNB-ACC-017 requires period locks and late-arriving treatment but not the concurrency rule between an in-flight posting and close.
business_problem: A posting validated against an open period can commit after a concurrent hard close (write skew), changing closed-period figures after statements issue.
statement: Every posting command MUST read the accounting period row for its posting date with a shared lock (or run SERIALIZABLE) in the posting transaction; HardClosePeriod MUST take an exclusive lock on that row. An ordinary posting whose posting date falls in a hard-closed period MUST be rejected with PERIOD_CLOSED, and the economic event MUST instead be recorded through a PriorPeriodAdjustment command that posts in the first open period, carries relates_to_period and effective_at of the original event, and requires controller approval above a sponsor-configured threshold. Routing is fixed by XID-EVA-002 and XID-ADV-005: before the audited statements for a year are issued, adjustments found in audit post in that year's AuditAdjustment period (UNB-XIN-ACC-005); after issuance, a late item posts as a PriorPeriodAdjustment classified Immaterial (current-period correction with disclosure) or Material (formal restatement of comparatives, originally issued statements preserved) against the sponsor's annual materiality setting agreed with the auditor; a hard-closed period MAY be reopened only before its statements are issued and only with controller and CFO approval. Donor fund statements already issued MUST show the correction as an explained adjustment on the next statement, and an amended statement MUST be issued whenever an acknowledgment or tax-relevant figure changes.
rationale: Closes a race that would otherwise silently alter issued financial statements.

discovery_source: Payment operations repair queues; workflow engines (rejected as infrastructure)
industry_analogy: Durable timers and process managers as database rows (outbox-driven), as in order-fulfilment systems
why_no_predecessor: DG-08 records the durable scheduler/timer gap; no requirement exists.
business_problem: Long-running DAF workflows (check aging, return windows, liquidation tranches, multi-leg funding, cooling-off, revalidation) lose state on restart and have no stuck detection.
statement: Each long-running business workflow MUST be implemented as a process manager persisted as a versioned row in the owning module's schema with: current step, expected next facts, next_due_at timer, attempt counts, and the ids of commands it has issued. A process manager MUST advance only by consuming authoritative facts or timer expiry, MUST issue commands with stable idempotency keys so re-execution after a crash has no duplicate effect, and MUST NOT hold database locks across external calls or AI invocations. Timers MUST be polled from the database (no in-memory-only timers). A process manager with no progress past its step SLA MUST create a ProcessManagerStalled item in the human-resolution queue with its state and last facts; humans resolve it only through domain commands. Outbox and fact-stream consumers MUST NOT infer missing events from gaps in database sequence values, and MUST NOT advance a read cursor past a position whose writing transaction may still commit (use claim-and-mark delivery with row locks, or a commit-ordered position such as a transaction-snapshot horizon).
rationale: Provides recovery without introducing a workflow engine or broker.

discovery_source: Public API versioning practice; widget integration (WG-8)
industry_analogy: SaaS platforms separate internal domain events from published webhooks

statement: Domain events MUST be classified private (consumed only inside the monolith) or published (delivered to partners, widgets or webhooks). discovery_source: Banking: asset freezes vs litigation holds vs OFAC blocks
industry_analogy: Banks distinguish legal hold on records, garnishment/freeze on funds and OFAC blocking into blocked accounts
why_no_predecessor: UNB-GAP-019 and UNB-GEX-038 mention legal holds within compliance cases; no requirement types the different holds or their blocked command sets.
business_problem: A shared hold abstraction over-blocks charitable distributions or under-blocks sanctioned payments.
statement: The system MUST model at least these distinct hold types with a declared set of blocked commands: ProtectiveHold(charity|recipient|destination) blocks release and dispatch to that subject; FundProtectiveFreeze blocks outflow commands from the fund (grants, transfers, and fee accrual only if sponsor policy says so) but MUST NOT block inbound contributions, dividends, valuation, statements or records access; SanctionsBlock moves affected funds to a blocked-property account and blocks unblocking without a licence/authorization record; RecordsLegalHold blocks only retention disposition and deletion. Each hold MUST record type, scope, authority, reason and release authority, and no hold type MAY be released by AI. During a dispute FundProtectiveFreeze (XID-EVA-004): fees continue to accrue; investments follow the standing policy but advisor-directed allocation changes are rejected; recurring and new grants are held; contributions may be accepted; nothing is distributed until the sponsor resolves the dispute.
rationale: Precise blocking prevents both over- and under-reaction.

discovery_source: Payment file processing; OFAC interdiction
industry_analogy: Payment hubs screen per item at release and again at transmission
parent_capability: Batch processing of grants and payments
why_no_predecessor: TVCTL-04 re-checks at submission and RR-REQ-X-020-r1 defines the hold version check, but nothing forbids batch-level approval or dispatch semantics.
business_problem: A recurring-grant run or payment file approved as a unit dispatches items after a mid-batch sanctions listing.
statement: A batch (recurring-grant run, payment file, statement run, fee run) MUST be a container of independent item commands and MUST NOT carry approval, release or dispatch authority itself. Each item MUST be committed in its own transaction with its own idempotency key and MUST record the HoldPublicationVersion it checked at release; the dispatcher MUST re-check each item immediately before transmitting it, including items already placed in an outbound file not yet transmitted. A hold published mid-run MUST stop all items not yet transmitted; the batch MUST end PartiallyCompleted with per-item outcomes.
rationale: Prevents batch abstraction from masking per-item legal gates.

Batch-level approval record used as item authority

argue_against: File rebuild before transmission adds latency.
simplest_valid_alternative: Re-check at file transmission only.
decision_rationale: Insufficient: item release must also not commit under a known hold.

discovery_source: Brokerage joint-account instruction authority; trust co-trustee rules
industry_analogy: Brokerages encode any-one vs all-signatories per account; conflicting orders are rejected or held
why_no_predecessor: ADM-023 requires detection and hold without defining conflict scope, precedence or the race with authority changes.
business_problem: Opposite instructions both execute, or every instruction is flagged.
statement: Each advisor instruction MUST carry a conflict scope key (fund, instruction kind, and target: charity, schedule, investment allocation or transfer). On commit, the handler MUST, in the same transaction, check for open instructions with the same scope from a different principal that request an incompatible outcome; if found, both MUST move to HeldConflict and a case opened for the sponsor, unless the fund's versioned instruction-authority policy (any-one, all, designated primary) resolves it deterministically. A one-off instruction for a scheduled occurrence MUST take precedence over the standing instruction only for that occurrence when sponsor policy says so. Every consequential command MUST compare the fund's authority epoch at commit with the epoch at recommendation; if it advanced (revocation, death notice, successor activation), unapproved recommendations MUST be held, and approved-reserved grants MUST follow the sponsor's in-flight policy.
rationale: Deterministic resolution for the common cases; humans only for true disputes.

argue_against: Scope keys need design per instruction kind.
simplest_valid_alternative: Hold all instructions when two advisors act within N hours.

discovery_source: Architecture governance; volume arithmetic from 15-economics and daf-landscape
industry_analogy: Capacity planning gates in payment processors
why_no_predecessor: REQ-X-020 item 10 requires measurements before a split but sets no threshold or metric.
business_problem: Without a threshold, brokers or services may be introduced on intuition or never introduced when needed.
statement: A message broker, separately deployed service or second authoritative store MUST NOT be introduced unless an ADR presents reproducible measurements on the selected managed PostgreSQL showing at least one of: (a) required peak authoritative commit rate exceeds 50% of benchmarked sustainable capacity of the largest sponsor database after indexing, partitioning and connection pooling; (b) p99 outbox dispatch lag exceeds 60 seconds for three consecutive peak days after tuning; (c) a contractual or regulatory clause requires an isolation profile that cannot be met inside the sponsor database (UNB-RCN-PLT-012). The benchmark MUST model the year-end peak of the largest expected sponsor using the documented volume method.
rationale: Converts the 'no distributed services without necessity' principle into a falsifiable gate.

discovery_source: CRM SaaS vs core banking customer master
industry_analogy: Banks separate legal account ownership/authority (core) from CRM engagement data
why_no_predecessor: UNB-PART-003 distinguishes roles but no requirement splits authority facts from engagement data or assigns storage/erasure semantics.
business_problem: CRM data could authorize actions, and immutable storage of engagement data conflicts with erasure.
statement: Relationship data MUST be classified as either (a) authority facts — advisory privilege grants and revocations, successor designations, contributor of record, anonymity and recognition elections, legal-representative evidence, consent records — owned by Identity & Delegation, stored append-only with effective/recorded times and checked synchronously by command handlers; or (b) engagement data — contact details, preferences, interests, interactions, segments, relationship-manager notes — owned by Donor & Sponsor Administration, stored as mutable rows with system-versioned history, eligible for privacy erasure/redaction, and NEVER read by a command handler to authorize or route money. Contact details used for mandatory notices MUST be read at send time with their version recorded.
rationale: Keeps the legal framing correct (sponsor controls assets; donors hold advisory privileges) and makes erasure feasible.

acceptance_criteria.given: A CRM note says 'Jane is now primary advisor'
acceptance_criteria.then: authorization uses Identity facts only; command rejected if no AdvisoryPrivilegeGranted for Jane

acceptance_criteria.given: Erasure request for a former advisor's interests and interaction notes
acceptance_criteria.then: engagement rows redacted with history entries; authority facts and grant records retained per retention class

failure_conditions: Command handler query touches crm schema

ai_automation: AI context for relationship managers uses engagement data under tenant scope.
ui_implications: CRM screens never present authority-changing controls.
api_implications: Separate APIs for authority and engagement.
reporting_implications: Engagement analytics separate from financial reporting.
priority_justification: Authorization integrity and legal correctness of who controls assets.
simplest_valid_alternative: Single party table with flags.
decision_rationale: Flags do not separate mutability or authorization paths.
priority_revision: Revised by adversarial review (XIF-ADV-003): Classification of data classes is architecture guidance; the P0 effect (CRM data never authorizes money) is already in RR-UNB-EVT-005-r1 and EVA-016.

discovery_source: Banking alerts (posted vs pending); e-commerce shipment notices
industry_analogy: Banks suppress 'payment sent' alerts when a payment is reversed before send
why_no_predecessor: UNB-RCN-PLT-002 catalogs notification events and ADV-088 forbids claiming Paid without confirmed state; nothing revalidates at send.
business_problem: Notices sent after the underlying fact changed state false finality or leak anonymity.
statement: Every notification derived from a fact MUST record the fact id and version it describes. Immediately before external send, the delivery worker MUST re-read the fact's current version and the recipient's anonymity/consent state; if the fact was superseded, reversed or returned, or the election changed so that the message would be false or disclosing, it MUST suppress the message (NotificationSuppressedAsSuperseded) and, for mandatory notices, enqueue the corrected notice instead.
rationale: Keeps communications truthful under eventual delivery.

acceptance_criteria.then: notice regenerated without donor identity

priority_justification: Customer obligations; prevents false statements to donors and charities.
simplest_valid_alternative: Delay non-urgent notices.
decision_rationale: Delay does not remove the race.

discovery_source: Core banking physical design; database privilege separation
industry_analogy: Banks keep postings, holds and customer data in separate tables with separate privileges
why_no_predecessor: RR-UNB-PLAT-007-r1 defines insert-only authoritative tables but does not forbid one generic event table holding all authority classes.
business_problem: A single generic event table prevents per-class privileges, constraints, retention and indexing.
statement: Records of different authority classes MUST be stored in physically separate tables (or schemas) with distinct database privileges: journal and reservation tables (financial facts, balance CHECK constraints), per-module authoritative fact tables, ai_observation (AI principal INSERT only here), external_observation (raw ingested evidence), outbox and process-manager tables (operational coordination, mutable), and engagement tables (mutable with history). A generic event or JSON-document table MAY be used only for outbox/integration delivery, and MUST NOT be the source of truth for any authoritative fact.
rationale: Lets the database enforce what code review alone cannot.

acceptance_criteria.when: attempts INSERT into ledger.journal_batch or grant.facts
acceptance_criteria.then: permission denied; incident logged

acceptance_criteria.given: Schema review
acceptance_criteria.when: a new table storing mixed fact types in a JSON column is proposed

AI role holds INSERT on fact tables

ai_automation: Enforces AI separation physically.
priority_justification: Strengthens enforcement of P0 controls; itself structural.
simplest_valid_alternative: Generic store with row-level policies per type.
decision_rationale: Harder to constrain (balanced journal CHECK, FKs).

discovery_source: Adversarial review (mission §16): cause "inability to profitably serve small accounts"; ECO worked example and economic-model cost per account
industry_analogy: Retail banking basic/limited-service accounts and 401(k) small-balance recordkeeping tiers: servicing obligations scale with account class, legal floors do not. Breaks down: a DAF fund is sponsor property, so service class may not affect legal controls, eligibility, sanctions or grant speed (XRJ-ECO-004).
why_no_predecessor: UNB-RCN-PLT-006 requires WorkItem-creating rules to state expected volume, and UNB-XIN-ECO-007/SAS-009 measure cost, but no requirement bounds the per-account recurring human, paper or vendor obligations a sponsor program imposes, and several new requirements (CRM-002, IAM-004, ERP-001, INV-006) add per-account recurring work universally.
business_problem: Fully loaded cost is ~$244-272 per account-year in Unbound's own models while low-balance accounts generate a few dollars of fee revenue; per-account recurring obligations make high-volume-low-balance and workplace programs structurally loss-making.
statement: Every account type MUST be assigned exactly one ServicingClass (Standard or DigitalMinimal) by sponsor policy. Every requirement-driven recurring per-account obligation (attestations, recertifications, outreach letters, printed statements, manual reviews not triggered by a legal or risk rule, vendor-priced checks) MUST be registered in a RecurringObligation register stating trigger, frequency, unit cost estimate with grade, legal basis class (statutory/regulatory, fiduciary, contractual, sponsor policy, risk control, convention) and per-class applicability. For DigitalMinimal accounts, obligations whose legal basis class is convention or sponsor policy MUST be event-triggered (on change or on a risk signal) rather than calendar-recurring, MUST use electronic delivery where consent exists, and the configured sum of expected recurring obligation cost per account-year MUST NOT exceed the sponsor-approved budget; publishing a program configuration that exceeds the budget MUST be rejected with the offending obligations listed. Obligations with legal basis statutory/regulatory, fiduciary or risk control MUST apply identically to all servicing classes, and ServicingClass MUST NOT be an input to eligibility, sanctions, approval, grant priority or payment timing.
applicability: tenant-configurable; required for high-volume-low-balance, embedded and workplace (REQ-X-070) programs
rationale: Makes the cost of each per-account duty visible and bounded at configuration time instead of discovering losses after launch, while preserving legal floors (PRINCIPLES step classification).

acceptance_criteria.given: a DigitalMinimal account type with an annual affiliation attestation obligation classed sponsor policy
acceptance_criteria.then: the obligation is converted to on-change/on-risk-signal triggering and no calendar task is scheduled for those accounts

acceptance_criteria.given: a program whose registered recurring obligations total an expected $9.40 per account-year against an approved budget of $6.00
acceptance_criteria.when: the sponsor administrator publishes the configuration
acceptance_criteria.then: publication is rejected listing each obligation, its unit cost and grade

acceptance_criteria.given: a DigitalMinimal and a Standard fund each recommending a grant to the same sanctioned-list match
acceptance_criteria.then: both receive identical sanctions and eligibility outcomes and timings, and the decision trace shows ServicingClass was not read

acceptance_criteria.given: an obligation registered without a legal basis class
acceptance_criteria.then: the save fails with a validation error

failure_conditions: A recurring obligation runs for DigitalMinimal accounts without a register entry
ServicingClass influences any legal, eligibility, sanctions or payment-timing decision
A statutory obligation is suppressed for DigitalMinimal accounts
security_compliance: Legal-basis classification of each obligation requires counsel review once per platform default pack (XID-ADV-010); servicing class excluded from decision inputs by type.
ai_automation: Deterministic; AI may draft obligation classification proposals for counsel review only.
ui_implications: Sponsor admin view of obligation register with per-account cost and budget gauge; DigitalMinimal donor UI is digital-only with clear statement of service scope.
api_implications: Program configuration publish API returns budget violations; account-type API exposes ServicingClass.
reporting_implications: Monthly expected vs actual recurring obligation cost per account by class (feeds ECO-007).
testing_requirements: Property test: for random grant inputs, outcomes are invariant to ServicingClass; configuration tests for budget rejection.
priority_justification: Without it a business model the platform claims to serve (high-volume-low-balance, workplace) cannot operate end to end on sustainable terms.
argue_for: Turns an invisible structural loss into a configuration-time decision; preserves legal floors.
argue_against: Unit cost estimates are illustrative until measured; sponsors may game classifications.
existing_capability_alternative: UNB-RCN-PLT-006 volume statements plus manual product review of each new obligation.
cost_and_hidden_complexity: One register and a publish-time check; requires each requirement owner to classify obligations once.
customer_friction: DigitalMinimal holders receive fewer reminders and no paper by default.
simplest_valid_alternative: Do not offer high-volume-low-balance programs in R1 (XID-ADV-002).
decision_rationale: Cheapest control that keeps the HVLB claim honest without weakening any legal control.
open_questions: Is a per-account cost budget compatible with sponsor fiduciary duties when the sponsor charges the same fee to all classes?
Which existing obligations are convention vs sponsor policy (counsel)?

discovery_source: Adversarial review: cause "inability to support large institutional clients"; contradiction ACC-010 vs EVA-001
industry_analogy: Fund administration shadow accounting: a shadow administrator reconciles to the official book and never publishes its own NAV. Breaks down: Unbound must still authorize grants, so it needs a capacity figure, not just a reconciliation.
parent_capability: Grant capacity and reservation when the ledger of record is external
why_no_predecessor: ACC-010 defines Shadow mode but only for reconciliation; EVA-001 and UNB-RCN-FIN-009 compute capacity from Unbound's own journal, which does not exist for Shadow functions.
business_problem: Institutional and outsourced-admin sponsors with an incumbent fund accountant cannot authorize grants in Unbound without either migrating their book of record or using an ungoverned balance.
statement: For a fund whose FundAttribution function is designated Shadow under UNB-XIN-ACC-010, grantable capacity MUST be computed as: the fund's available balance in the latest external snapshot accepted as complete under UNB-XIN-EVA-004 (with its as-of watermark) minus all Unbound reservations and released-unsettled grants committed after that watermark minus accrued-unposted fees reported by the external system. Reservations MUST be committed in Unbound's reservation table under the same locking rules as Authoritative funds. When the snapshot watermark is older than the sponsor-configured staleness limit (default 1 business day) the system MUST block capacity increases and new reservations above a sponsor-configured de minimis amount, while permitting protective actions. Each daily reconciliation break between the external balance and (prior snapshot - Unbound-originated settled outflows since) MUST open a reconciliation case and MUST freeze new reservations for the affected fund until resolved or accepted by the controller.
rationale: Gives Shadow-mode clients a deterministic, auditable capacity source without a second balance ledger.

acceptance_criteria.given: a Shadow fund with external available balance $100,000 at watermark T and Unbound reservations of $30,000 committed after T
acceptance_criteria.then: the reservation is rejected for insufficient capacity ($70,000 available) in the same transaction

acceptance_criteria.given: the latest complete external snapshot is 2 business days old with a 1-day limit
acceptance_criteria.when: a new recommendation above the de minimis amount is approved
acceptance_criteria.then: it is held with reason SHADOW_SNAPSHOT_STALE and a SourceFeedGapDetected case exists

acceptance_criteria.given: a reconciliation break of $4,200 on a Shadow fund
acceptance_criteria.then: a case opens, new reservations for that fund are frozen, and existing approved grants follow the in-flight policy

acceptance_criteria.given: a Shadow fund
acceptance_criteria.when: any command attempts to post a fund-attribution journal in Unbound
acceptance_criteria.then: the command is rejected per ACC-010

failure_conditions: Capacity computed from a snapshot not accepted as complete
Reservations committed after the watermark omitted from the deduction
Shadow fund journals posted in Unbound
security_compliance: Snapshot ingestion integrity (control totals) per EVA-004; controller-only acceptance of breaks.
ai_automation: Deterministic; AI may summarize reconciliation breaks for the controller.
ui_implications: Donor-visible available balance labelled with as-of time; staff view of watermark age.
api_implications: Capacity API returns watermark and staleness state.
reporting_implications: Fund statements in Shadow mode are issued by the external book of record; Unbound reports reservations and grants only.
testing_requirements: Interleaving tests of snapshot arrival vs reservation commits; stale-feed simulations.
priority_justification: Essential end-to-end grant operations for institutional and outsourced-admin clients that keep an external book of record.
argue_for: Unblocks the largest clients without a second ledger.
argue_against: Introduces dependency on external feed timeliness; adds a second capacity formula.
existing_capability_alternative: Require institutional clients to migrate their book of record before go-live.
cost_and_hidden_complexity: A second capacity path to test; reconciliation staffing at the sponsor.
customer_friction: Balances may lag one business day; stale feeds pause new grants.
simplest_valid_alternative: Disallow Shadow FundAttribution (migration-first onboarding).
decision_rationale: Shadow mode was proposed (ACC-010) without a capacity source; this closes the contradiction with EVA-001.
open_questions: Do any target institutional sponsors actually require Shadow FundAttribution, or only Shadow GL?
Default de minimis amount and staleness limit.
